mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Interpret any phrase of the form 'the difference between the number of X and Y' as the signed subtraction X - Y, preserving order, rather than as an absolute value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement uses the phrase 'difference between the number of X and Y' (or similar) to relate counts.
mathgap.example: Treating 'the difference between the number of apples and oranges' as |apples - oranges| and setting both counts equal, ignoring sign.

mathgap.title: Directed More-Than Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate statements like 'A has N more (or fewer) items than B' into the equation A = B + N (or A = B - N), keeping the direction of the comparison.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement explicitly says one person has more or fewer items than another.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'A has 3 more items than B' as A = B - 3, subtracting instead of adding.

mathgap.title: Immediate Direct Assignment Update
mathgap.principle: When a direct count statement 'A has N items' appears, set A's current count to N at that moment, overwriting any previous value, because later operations may modify it.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement provides an explicit count for a person.
mathgap.example: Ignoring a later transfer that changes A's count after setting A = 5 from an earlier direct assignment.

mathgap.title: Temporal Consistency of Transfers and Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: Process statements in the order given; apply each transfer immediately before evaluating any later relational statements, ensuring that later statements see the updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any sequence of statements that includes transfers and relational constraints.
mathgap.example: Evaluating a comparison that mentions a person's count before a preceding transfer has been applied, leading to an outdated value.

mathgap.title: Full Difference Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: For statements equating one difference to another, translate them into (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the signed order on both sides, rather than assigning one side to the other variable.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says 'the difference between X and Y equals the difference between U and V' (or similar).
mathgap.example: Converting 'X - Y = Z' into X = Z and ignoring Y, which loses the subtraction relationship.

mathgap.title: Quantity Modification (Multiplication and Subtraction)
mathgap.principle: When a statement modifies a count by a numeric operation other than direct assignment or transfer (e.g., 'increases by 2 times', 'decreases by 3'), apply the operation to the current count, treating 'increase by N times' as multiplication by N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement describes a change using verbs like 'increase', 'decrease', 'multiply', or phrases like 'increases by N times'.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'increase by 2 times' as adding 2 instead of multiplying by 2.

mathgap.title: Conditional Transfer of All Items
mathgap.principle: If a transfer statement says a person gives all their items to another, possibly conditioned on a threshold (e.g., 'If X has more than N items'), first evaluate the condition using the current count; if the condition holds, set the giver’s count to zero and add the transferred amount to the recipient.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement involves a full transfer of items, especially with an 'if' clause.
mathgap.example: Executing 'If Arianna has more than 5 cucumbers, Arianna will transfer their cucumbers to Adele' even when Arianna has only 1 cucumber.

mathgap.title: Complete Statement Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify and extract every statement that mentions the target item (direct counts, differences, transfers, redistributions, conditionals) before attempting to solve, ensuring no constraint is omitted.
mathgap.when_to_apply: At the start of solving any problem, before processing constraints.
mathgap.example: Stopping after processing the first ten statements and ignoring later constraints that affect the queried person.

mathgap.title: Split All Items Equally Among Recipients
mathgap.principle: When a statement says a person splits all their items equally among two or more recipients, set the giver’s count to zero and add an equal share of the original amount to each recipient (original count divided by the number of recipients).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever phrasing like 'splits all the X she owns equally among A and B' appears.
mathgap.example: Treating 'Benito splits all the cucumbers she owns equally among Sylvester and Royce' as giving all cucumbers to Sylvester only, leaving Royce unchanged.

mathgap.title: Redistribute Equally Among Group
mathgap.principle: When a statement says two or more persons redistribute their items to ensure each has an equal amount, compute the total among those persons at that moment, divide by the number of persons, and set each person's count to that equal share (assuming integer division).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When phrasing like 'X and Y redistribute their cucumbers to ensure each has an equal amount' appears.
mathgap.example: Leaving Pamela and Fay with their original counts instead of giving each half of their combined total after 'Pamela and Fay redistribute their cucumbers to ensure each has an equal amount.'

mathgap.description: Treating ‘difference between the number of X and Y’ as absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model defaults to interpreting 'difference' as a magnitude, ignoring the order of terms.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of the named variables and compute X - Y, not |X - Y|.

mathgap.description: Delaying the effect of transfer statements until after all other statements.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model processes relational constraints first and postpones transfers, breaking temporal ordering.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer immediately when its statement is encountered, before any later relational statements.

mathgap.description: Considering a direct count as a fixed initial value that cannot be changed by later transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats direct assignments as immutable, overlooking subsequent operations.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat direct counts as the current value at that moment, which can be altered by later transfers or modifications.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting a difference equality as a direct assignment to a single variable, ignoring the second term.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model simplifies an equation like (A - B) = (C - D) to A = C, dropping the subtraction.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate difference equalities fully as (A - B) = (C - D) and solve for the variables accordingly.

mathgap.description: Incomplete processing of problem statements: stopping after a subset of constraints or ignoring many statements.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may truncate parsing due to length or perceived irrelevance.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Systematically extract and process every statement before solving.
